name: Facial Blood Flow Detection
description: Detects subtle facial color changes from blood flow (rPPG) — real faces show pulse signals absent in AI-generated faces.
mechanism:
This method detects deepfakes by analyzing remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) — the subtle skin color changes caused by blood flow that are present in real faces but absent or artificially reproduced in deepfakes:

1. **ROI Selection and Signal Extraction**: The method tracks facial landmarks across video frames and extracts spatially averaged RGB signals from blood-flow-sensitive regions: forehead, left cheek, right cheek, and chin. These regions are chosen because they have dense capillary networks close to the skin surface. The raw RGB temporal signals are decomposed using chrominance-based rPPG methods (CHROM algorithm, de Haan & Jeanne, 2013) that combine color channels to maximize pulse signal and suppress motion artifacts: S = 3R − 2G (projection that isolates hemoglobin absorption variations from specular reflections and illumination changes).

2. **Pulse Signal Quality Assessment**: The extracted rPPG signal is bandpass filtered (0.7–4.0 Hz, corresponding to 42–240 BPM) and analyzed for pulse signal quality. Real faces produce a quasi-periodic signal with: (a) a dominant frequency in the 0.8–2.5 Hz range (normal resting heart rate), (b) signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) above 3 dB, (c) harmonic structure — the power spectrum shows peaks at the fundamental frequency and its 2nd/3rd harmonics. Deepfakes typically show no dominant pulse frequency, SNR below 0 dB, and flat power spectra. The method computes a pulse quality index (PQI) combining these features.

3. **Spatial Coherence of Pulse Signal**: In real faces, the pulse signal is spatially coherent — the same heartbeat drives blood flow in all facial regions, so rPPG signals from forehead, left cheek, right cheek, and chin should be highly correlated (cross-correlation > 0.7) with physiologically plausible time delays (< 50 ms between regions). Deepfakes that attempt to simulate blood flow often fail to maintain spatial coherence — they may inject pulse-like signals that are not synchronized across regions, show different frequencies in different ROIs, or exhibit phase relationships that violate hemodynamic physics.

4. **Heart Rate Variability (HRV) Analysis**: Real rPPG signals exhibit natural heart rate variability — the interval between successive pulse peaks varies according to autonomic nervous system activity. The method computes HRV features: SDNN (standard deviation of normal-to-normal intervals), RMSSD (root mean square of successive differences), and the LF/HF ratio (low-frequency to high-frequency power ratio). Authentic HRV shows SDNN of 30–100 ms and RMSSD of 20–60 ms. Deepfakes that inject synthetic pulse signals typically show either zero HRV (perfectly periodic signal) or unrealistic HRV patterns (random interval variations without physiological structure).
parameters:
rPPG algorithm: CHROM (de Haan & Jeanne, 2013)
ROI regions: forehead, left cheek, right cheek, chin
Bandpass filter: 0.7–4.0 Hz (Butterworth 6th order)
Pulse quality index threshold: PQI > 0.5 indicates real face
SNR threshold: > 3 dB for valid pulse detection
Spatial coherence threshold: cross-correlation > 0.7
Phase delay limit: < 50 ms between facial regions
Minimum video duration: 5 seconds (≥ 5 cardiac cycles)
Frame rate requirement: ≥ 25 fps
Minimum face resolution: 96×96 pixels
accuracy: 85–94% accuracy distinguishing real from deepfake faces via rPPG analysis. Pulse quality index achieves AUC of 0.92 on FaceForensics++ dataset. Spatial coherence analysis provides F1-score of 0.90. HRV features add 3–5% improvement. Performance degrades significantly with heavy video compression (CRF > 35) and low frame rates (< 15 fps).
source: Ciftci, U. A. et al. (2020). FakeCatcher: Detection of Synthetic Portrait Videos using Biological Signals. IEEE TPAMI, 42(10), 2607–2622.
useCase: Detecting face swap and face reenactment deepfakes through absence of biological signals. Real-time deepfake detection in video conferencing. Identity verification supplementing facial recognition. Forensic analysis of video evidence for court proceedings.
strengths:
• Exploits fundamental biological difference — real faces have blood flow, synthetic faces don't
• Spatial coherence analysis is robust against simple pulse injection attacks
• HRV analysis detects sophisticated synthetic pulse signals
• Non-invasive and works with standard video cameras
• Independent of face generation method — targets biological authenticity
limitations:
• Requires minimum 5 seconds of video at ≥ 25 fps
• Heavy video compression destroys subtle color variations
• Dark skin tones produce weaker rPPG signals (higher melanin absorption)
• Subject motion and illumination changes degrade signal quality
• Advanced deepfakes may incorporate learned rPPG simulation
